_comment: Copy to data/mcp.json (gitignored). Latch is an approval-gating MCP HOST: it connects to these MCP servers (which hold their own credentials in 'env'); the worker never sees them. The worker can only REQUEST a tool call, which becomes an 'mcp_tool_call' approval; the trusted host runs it after you approve. Set MCP_ENABLED=1 or enabled:true to turn it on.

servers.name: filesystem
servers.description: Read/list files under an allowed directory

servers.name: bureau
servers.description: An MCP server reached over HTTP rather than spawned. The era it speaks (legacy 2025-06-18 vs modern 2026-07-28) is PROBED at runtime, not configured -- see MCP-PROTOCOL-SUPPORT.md.

servers.name: example-with-secret
servers.description: An MCP server that needs an API key (kept on the host, never on the worker)

_fields.transport: 'stdio' spawns the server as a subprocess and speaks JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout; 'http' POSTs JSON-RPC to 'url'; 'mock' is for tests. stdio is legacy-era only; http negotiates legacy or modern by probing.
_fields.url: http transport only. The JSON-RPC endpoint. Latch probes it with server/discover to decide which MCP era it speaks, and caches that per server for 60s.
_fields.headers: http transport only. Credentials for the endpoint -- what 'env' is to a spawned command. Kept on the host; the operator API reports header KEY NAMES and never values.
_fields.allowRemote: http transport only, default false. Must be true before Latch will POST to a non-loopback host. Sending operator credentials off this machine is a different act from spawning a local subprocess, so it is declared rather than implied by giving a URL -- a mistyped hostname then fails closed instead of posting a bearer token somewhere unintended. Such a server is badged 'remote credentials' in the MCP panel.
_fields.command_args: Pin the server to an explicit version rather than letting a floating fetch pull the latest -- e.g. '@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@X.Y.Z' instead of the bare package name. An unpinned 'npx -y pkg' re-resolves to the newest release on every spawn, so a compromised or rug-pulled upstream release silently becomes the server you vetted. Pinning (plus a lockfile or registry mirror) is the supply-chain control.
_fields.allowedTools: Optional. If non-empty, ONLY these tool names may be called on this server. Empty = allow any tool the server exposes (still approval-gated).
_fields.autoApprove: Optional. Tool names pre-authorised for autonomy auto-approval (Full access only). Still audited. Leave empty to require a human for every call. Auto-approval is bound to the tool's fingerprint (name + description + inputSchema): if the server later changes that tool's description or schema, the fingerprint no longer matches and the call falls back to a human approval instead of auto-running -- blocking the MCP tool-poisoning / rug-pull vector where a trusted tool's description is mutated into an injection payload after you allowlisted it.
_fields.argConstraints: Optional per-tool argument bounds enforced host-side before the call runs, for tools that don't self-sandbox. Per field: {"prefix":"..."} | {"equals":value} | {"enum":[...]}. Tool arguments are also validated against the tool's own inputSchema regardless.
